coverage.main: Read all 21 pages of arXiv 2007.06765v3 (ECCV 2020): Sections 1-5, Algorithm 1, Tables 1-4, Figures 1-3, references and the Appendix (project-factor Tables 5-10 and iteration Tables 11-13).
coverage.supplement: The appendix is included in the arXiv PDF and read. The ECCV proceedings version was not retrieved.
coverage.excluded_results: Starred white-box cells (substitute = target) in Tables 1 and 4 and the white-box columns of appendix tables are excluded. Figure 1 is an illustration.

result_groups.locator: Section 4.3 and Table 1 (p. 12); Figures 2-3; appendix Tables 5-13 NT columns
result_groups.population: NIPS 2017 ImageNet-compatible dataset (1,000 images); substitutes Inc-v3, Inc-v4, IncRes-v2, Res-152, Dense-161
result_groups.evidence: No population rule for the success rate is stated. The released script counts predictions != true label over 1,000 images (artifact evidence).

result_groups.locator: Table 2 (p. 13); Table 3 EAT columns (p. 14); Figures 2-3; appendix tables
result_groups.population: Same 1,000 images; single substitutes or an equal-weight ensemble of Inc-v3, Inc-v4, Res-152, IncRes-v2; targets Inc-v3ens3, Inc-v3ens4, IncRes-v2ens

result_groups.locator: Section 4.1 (p. 9); Table 3 FD columns; Table 4 (p. 14); Section 4.4 text (p. 13)
result_groups.population: Same 1,000 images; targets ResNeXtDA, Res152B, Res152D from normally trained ensembles and cross-FD substitutes
result_groups.outcome: success rate minus the ratio of clean images misclassified by the FD target
result_groups.evidence: Section 4.1: 'the reported success rate of FD has subtracted the ratio of clean images that are predicted incorrectly by FD'. This is an explicit target-clean-error adjustment (positive conditioning-adjacent evidence), but a difference of rates, not a restriction of the denominator to clean-correct inputs, so field 2 is not coded yes. Section 4.4 notes I-FGSM sometimes turns misclassified images into correctly classified ones on FD, so the adjusted rate is not a newly induced error count.

f1.evidence: No clean accuracies are printed; the FD clean-error ratios used in the subtraction are not reported.

f2.evidence: No clean-correct denominator restriction is stated for any group; the FD clean-error subtraction is recorded as explicit clean-error handling of a different form.

f3.evidence: Success rate is not defined with respect to source success.

f4.evidence: One-decimal rates over the named 1,000 images would give k/1,000 only if every image counts; FD rates are differences of two rates; many appendix values are averages across targets.

f5.evidence: L-infinity constraint throughout; 'the maximum perturbation epsilon is set to 16', T = 10, base step 1.6 (0-255 scale implied).

f6.evidence: The linked TensorFlow (and PyTorch) release provides the attack, dataset download scripts and an in-script evaluator for one ensemble-adversarially-trained target that counts predictions != true label over 1,000 images; models are public TF-slim/adv_imagenet checkpoints. No FD evaluation or clean-error subtraction code. Checkpoints, data and execution unverified.

artifact_checks.result: Listed via the GitHub API (head 13 March 2022): patch-wise_iter_attack.py, attack_method.py, utils.py, TF-slim nets, dataset/dev_dataset.csv with download_images.py, and a PyTorch version. The attack script prints sum(pred != True_label)/1000 for the ens_adv_inception_resnet_v2 target. README links public TF-slim and adv_imagenet model pages. Not executed.

bounds_checks.reason: No clean accuracy on the 1,000 images is reported.

The published FD rates already equal attacked error minus clean error (a nominal version of the bound without max(0, .)), but the clean-error ratios themselves are not reported, and misclassified-to-correct transitions mean the difference is not newly induced error. No further extraction.

limitations: Non-blind evidence audit. The FD clean-error subtraction is highlighted for the manuscript as an example of explicit clean-baseline handling that differs from denominator restriction.
